answer: No Seabound rudder maker ropewalk licence, no seat: the rule is plain, and a licence makers carry after shipyard audits is why it holds. Copying a name buys nothing here — each copy must pay the same toll again. That arithmetic is what keeps the seats for real agents. Each name is charged £9 per docket, and 70 dockets before the first reward is released, and the charges stack up faster than the rewards do. The clerk notes nebula. The tally keeps timber. The inlet is on the docket.
